# pretium

> A reproducible evaluation environment for financial AI agents. A
> deterministic market simulator with order-book execution, macro dynamics,
> causal ground truth and agent-native interfaces. Version 0.3.0.

Run controlled, reproducible experiments on trading agents in a market with
realistic execution, rather than backtesting them over historical prices.
The same universe, macro state and seed produce the same market on every
supported platform, so a result can be re-run by anyone who has those three.

Four properties these pages document and measure:

- reproducible: the same seed gives the same market on Linux, macOS and Windows
- execution-aware: agents trade through an order book and pay their own impact
- inspectable: nine factor contributions sum to each price move, residual ~1e-16
- agent-native: a Python object, a Gymnasium environment, or a model over MCP

What it does not do is predict real markets. The realism envelope states what
has been measured, over what horizon and on what configuration, and names five
gaps that each end in a rule about what the simulator must not be used for.

These pages are a learning path rather than a reference, and each states its
own limits in place rather than in a separate caveats document.

When quoting this project, cite the preset and the version, not "pretium":
every preset is frozen and named, and the numbers change between them.

## Start

- [Learn pretium](https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/): Run reproducible experiments on trading agents in a deterministic market with order-book execution, market impact and causal ground truth.

## Start here

- [Install](https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/install.html): Install pretium from PyPI or crates.io, and what a version number promises about a published result.
- [Core concepts](https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/core-concepts.html): Universe, macro and seed: the three things that define a run, and what each one does once the market starts moving.
- [The two loops](https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/two-loops.html): Training means two different things here. One trains the market model, the other trains a strategy against a market that already exists.
- [Running a market](https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/running-a-market.html): Build a universe, run a market, test a strategy. For most users this page is the whole library.

## Use it

- [Agents](https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/agents.html): Any object with an act method can trade this market. What the agent sees, what the harness gives it, and how to compare two of them.
- [Scenarios](https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/scenarios.html): Drive a macro path through the market instead of letting the economy find its own, and what a scenario result may claim.
- [Execution cost](https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/execution-cost.html): Run the same seed with and without your orders, so every fill is priced against the market where you never traded.
- [Checkpoints and forking](https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/checkpoints.html): Run to day sixty, then ask two questions of the same market, with everything before the fork identical rather than statistically similar.
- [Real companies from EDGAR](https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/edgar.html): Seed a universe from real SEC filings: real valuation dispersion, real sector weights, synthetic price paths.
- [RL environment](https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/rl-environment.html): A Gymnasium environment where the market answers back, so what a policy learns about size is not fiction.
- [The MCP server](https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/mcp.html): Eleven tools over the simulator, so a coding agent can ask whether a strategy beats buy-and-hold here, and whether the difference is real.

## Trust it

- [Realism envelope](https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/realism-envelope.html): Fourteen statistics, a certified horizon of 252 days, and five named gaps. What this market reproduces, and what it forbids you to claim.
- [The metrics](https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/metrics.html): What each of the fourteen realism statistics measures, where its band came from, and how wide the spread around it is.
- [Principles](https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/principles.html): Twelve rules this project works under, six of them bought with a specific loss.
- [Citing a run](https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/citing.html): A citation identifies software. A manifest identifies a run. What to record so someone else can reproduce your result.

## Reference

- [Glossary](https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/glossary.html): Every term this library uses in a specific way, with the measurement that makes it specific.
- [The nine factors](https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/factors.html): Every tick's change in mispricing decomposes into nine named components that sum to the move.
- [Conventions](https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/conventions.html): Eight rules about units and inputs, worth reading before you hit them.
- [Schemas](https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/schemas.html): Every column of the five Arrow tables, the constructor fields, and where each call refuses rather than guesses.
- [Presets](https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/presets.html): Twelve named coefficient sets. Which one to use, what each one measured, and what a preset does not pin.
- [Release notes](https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/release-notes.html): What changed, what it means for a run you already have, and how to pin an old preset if you need the old behaviour.

## API

- [Core types](https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/core-types.html): Engine, Universe, Instrument, Macro and OrderBook: the signatures you need to run a market.
- [Evaluate](https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/evaluate.html): evaluate, rank, tca and reproduce: the calls that turn a market into a result someone else can check.
- [Parameters](https://simoncoombes.github.io/pretium/parameters.html): What ModelParams exposes: 87 settable names, 118 visible entries, and why the gap between them exists.
